Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week — ClearPath is excited about Redwood for inference at scale. Procurement here is pulling together the commercial ask so we can compare with other bidders. A few clarifying questions up front:

- Can you provide an itemized breakdown: one-time onboarding/NRE, recurring platform fee (how you tier it), per-token/meters if applicable, and the support tiers (what is included in Bronze/Silver/Gold)?
- Do you have a standard migration credit or SOW-based credit for lift & onboarding? If so, how is that typically booked (one-time credit vs amortized platform fee reduction)?
- For VPC/on-prem installs we need language around entitlements (number of hosts / GPU counts) and whether we offer burst/bandwidth overage.
- High-level discount guidance for a 12–24 month committed path vs a 6-month pilot would help.

I attached our RFP (ClearPath_RFP_062020.pdf) with preferred pricing tables and a draft procurement checklist. Can we get a written response by EOD Monday? If helpful we can set a 30-min sync.

Best,

Alex — thanks for the RFP and the clear list. Quick response to get the conversation moving and then I'll send a more detailed packet + pricing spreadsheet:

- High-level structure: onboarding (one-time NRE), platform fee (recurring annual or monthly), optional usage metering for token-heavy workloads, and three support tiers (Standard / Enhanced / Premium) with varying response SLAs and included on-call hours.
- Migration credits: we can offer either a one-time migration credit applied to the first invoice or an amortized platform fee reduction over the first 6–12 months. We typically prefer a structured, milestone-based credit (SOW-tied) for larger projects.
- Entitlements: licensing maps to reserved GPU capacity (sku counts) with a defined burst policy. We can include a capped burst allowance or pre-purchase burst credits.
- Discounting: pilot (6 months) — smaller introductory discount (single-digit). 12–24m committed — tiered discounts, larger for multi-year.

I'm attaching a quick pricing workbook (Redwood_VPC_pricing_v1.xlsx) with a few model scenarios. Would you prefer a short call Monday morning to walk that together?

Thanks — I'll loop in pricing and commercial for scenario building.

—Tessa Morgan

Need your recommended counter to present Monday afternoon. Key constraints: ClearPath wants predictable TCO, migration support, and a reasonable burst model.

Szenarios (very high-level):
1) Baseline (Commercial Tiers): 16% platform fee (annual), NRE as billed; Standard support. No migration credit.
2) Strategic (1-yr commit): 12% platform fee (25% off list for platform fee), $75k migration credit (SOW-tied), Enhanced support (8x5 on-call + 24h SLA).
3) Enterprise (2-yr commit + larger GPU reserve): 10% platform fee (35% off list), $150k migration credit, Premium support (24x7 + designated TAM + 4 hours/week on-call).

Questions for pricing:
- Do we prefer to offer migration credit as upfront credit or amortized across invoices?
- Recommend a middle-ground counter we can reasonably sign without exec uplift?

Pls reply inline. I need a clean counter to send to Alex by EOD Monday.

Attaching scenario_calc_0620.csv

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: ClearPath RFP — pricing scenarios (need recommendation)

Tessa — quick thoughts inline.

- Migration credit: prefer SOW-tied milestone credit paid against invoices (keeps accounting clean). Cap absolute $ amount but allow refund if milestones not met.
- Platform fee vs amortization: rather than a straight % off, propose a short-term amortization (first 6 mo at 50% platform fee) + a one-time migration credit. This avoids long-term list erosion but gives them runway.
- Support tiers (recommended naming and bullets):
  - Standard: 9x5 email support, 48h response, access to docs and community forums.
  - Enhanced: 9x5 phone + email, 24h response, 8 on-call hrs/month, quarterly business reviews.
  - Premium: 24x7 phone + email, 4 on-call hrs/week, dedicated TAM, monthly QBRs, SLA credits for P1s.

Counter proposal (what I recommend we send):
- 18% effective platform fee for 12-month reserved capacity (reflects list discounts + short amortization).
- Migration credit: $50k SOW-tied, applied against first two invoices (milestone schedule in SOW).
- Support: Enhanced included; Premium available as add-on at 30% uplift.
- Burst: include 10% free burst capacity per month; additional used burst billed at metered rates with 14d notice.

This keeps us competitive and preserves long-term list. No exec uplift needed for these numbers.

—Marissa

Alex — thanks for the RFP and for the patience while we modeled options. Below is our recommended counter based on ClearPath's priorities (predictable cost, migration support, burst flexibility). If that looks reasonable I can get Legal to draft a short commercial term sheet and SOW and circulate for signature.

Redwood counter (high level):
- Term & commitment: 12-month reserved capacity (SKU-based GPU commit).
- Platform fee: effective 18% annual platform fee on committed capacity (applies to reserved units).
- Migration support: $50,000 migration credit, SOW-tied to completion of two onboarding milestones; credit applied to first two invoices.
- Support: Enhanced tier included (9x5 phone & email, 24h response SLA, 8 on-call hrs/month). Premium (24x7 + TAM) available as an add-on at 30% uplift.
- Burst policy: 10% monthly burst included; excess billed at metered overage rates with 14-day notice and option to convert to reserved capacity.
- Billing & invoicing: platform fee billed monthly in arrears; migration credit deducted on invoices per SOW schedule.

Attachments: Redwood-ClearPath-Counter-0622.pdf (term summary)

Next steps:
1) Confirm you want to proceed with the above — I'll loop Legal for a short commercial term sheet.
2) We draft SOW with milestone schedule for migration credit.
3) Execute Commercial + SOW via DocuSign; target signature within 2 weeks to hit July onboarding window.

If helpful, I'm available for a 30-min call tomorrow morning to walk the numbers.
